name: Jorge Chávez International Airport
before:
Peru's main airport and one of the largest in South America, in Callao 11 km north west of the historic centre of Lima and 17 km from Miraflores. It handled 22,876,785 passengers in 2023.

This airport has changed completely and recently, so older guidance is unreliable. A second runway and a new control tower came into service in April 2023, and an entirely new passenger terminal opened on 1 June 2025, replacing the old one. The old terminal was going to become a logistics centre, but as of July 2025 the government was weighing reopening it to add capacity.

There are two Wyndham hotels on site. The new Wyndham Grand Costa del Sol sits in front of the new terminal, opened in June 2025, its design drawn from the textile patterns of the Paracas culture. The original Costa del Sol, built with noise cancelling panels in 2007, stays open by the old terminal.

The airport is owned by Fraport and run by Lima Airport Partners. It is named after Jorge Chávez, the Peruvian aviator.
after:
Peru's main airport and one of the largest in South America, in Callao 11 km north west of the historic centre of Lima. It handled more than 25 million passengers in 2025.

This airport has changed completely and recently, so older guidance is unreliable. A second runway and a new control tower came into service in April 2023, and a new passenger terminal opened on 1 June 2025, replacing the old one.

Of the two Costa del Sol Wyndham hotels, the new Wyndham Grand sits in front of the new terminal. The original stays open by the old terminal, and Costa del Sol says it is 5.3 km from the new one, with a free shuttle every 30 minutes.

Lima Airport Partners runs the airport under a state concession, and Fraport owns 80.01 per cent of that company. It is named after Jorge Chávez, a pioneer of Peruvian aviation.

claims.claim: more than 25 million passengers in 2025
claims.inAfter: It handled more than 25 million passengers in 2025.
claims.note: Replaces the 2023 figure (22,876,785). Good sources disagree on the 2025 total, so the text gives the floor both support. Fraport's 2025 annual report counts 25,496,109 (commercial traffic only, in, out and transit), a record, up 4.1 per cent on 2024's 24,495,815. Wikipedia's infobox gives 27,420,159 for 2025, citing CORPAC; CORPAC's own national tables say they include regular, non-regular, general aviation and military flights, which may explain the gap. CORPAC's per-airport figures are only in a spreadsheet download that the sweep's tools cannot save as text. Both figures are above 25 million. For Andy: the 25.5 million record could go in, attributed to Fraport.
